subject: constrain shape parameters >0 in beta distribution

messages.author: a9e2e9ac319971b0
messages.subject: constrain shape parameters >0 in beta distribution
parts:
Hi all, I am working on a beta distribution model following the reparameterization method in the manual. 
my beta distribution model is something like:

for (n in 1:N){
    mu_x[n] <- dot_product(row(mu,id[n]),row(x,n));  //x is data, mu is the coefficient I want to estimate
   
    inv_mu <- inv_logit(mu_x[n]);  //inv_mu is mean of beta distribution
    a <- inv_mu * pi ;
    b <- (1.0 - inv_mu) * pi;
   }

 increment_log_prob(beta_log(y, a, b))
 

However, I still got warnings after sampling saying "the shape parameter is 0, but must be >0!", so my question is how to constrain the shape parameter so that a & b >0 , or is there a better way to reparameterize beta distribution?

Thanks!!

Haoyan

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: constrain shape parameters >0 in beta distribution
parts:
On Monday, May 2, 2016 at 2:44:06 PM UTC-4, Haoyan Sun wrote:
However, I still got warnings after sampling saying "the shape parameter is 0, but must be >0!", so my question is how to constrain the shape parameter so that a & b >0 , or is there a better way to reparameterize beta distribution?

I think you need to declare

real<lower=0> pi;

in parameters.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: constrain shape parameters >0 in beta distribution
parts:
On Monday, May 2, 2016 at 3:31:35 PM UTC-4, Haoyan Sun wrote:
I didn't write out the parameter section in my question above, but I do declare pi as you suggested, otherwise I wouldn't even have sampling finished.
So the sampling finishes ok, my problem is just the warning message that some shape parameter is 0. I don't know if I should just ignore the warning or there is a better way to reparametrize.

If you have it parameterized like that, then the problem is simply that on some transitions pi underflowed to zero. In that case, it will reject the proposal but if it only happens a few times, it is not a big deal. You can perhaps avoid it by putting some prior on pi with vanishing density at zero.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: constrain shape parameters >0 in beta distribution
parts:
You probably want that Pareto the other way around if it's to
match the manual. That's the uniform on the log scale prior
that Andrew recommended in BDA. He told me he doesn't like
that prior any more, but as far as I know, hasn't suggested
an alternative. Probably because we almost always work on
the log-odds scale rather than directly with beta variates.

Also, if you have pi ~ pareto(epsilon, 1.5), then you
need to declare

parameters<lower=epsilon> pi;

because that first parameter in the pareto is the lower bound.

- Bob
